title: Loops & iteration
outcome: Process a collection reliably, preserving order and boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Walk a sequence
steps.text: A for loop visits items. range(stop) excludes stop. Decide whether you need values, positions, or both.

steps.title: 2. Carry state
steps.text: An accumulator begins with an identity: zero for addition, [] for collected results. Initialize per-call state before the loop, not inside it.

steps.title: 3. Stop or skip deliberately
steps.text: break stops the loop; continue skips one iteration. A while loop must move toward a terminating condition.

steps.title: 4. Combine sequences
steps.text: zip pairs by position and normally stops at the shorter input. Validate equal lengths when the contract needs them. Nested loops create combinations; they are not a substitute for pairing.

steps.title: 5. Check empty and partial data
steps.text: The empty case is part of the contract. A loop that records no fault is not proof that any device was actually checked.

tasks.title: Safe countdown
contract: data is a nonnegative int. result is [data,data-1,...,1], empty for zero. Use a while loop.

    n += 1
